statement: In the 10-Q for 2023-09-30 the filer put three subtotal figures on the wrong members: the Wholesale subtotal (35,982) and the Transportation: Cargo subtotal (65,402) are tagged on each other's members, and the Second Lien Debt section total (219,547) is tagged on the Second Lien Debt Telecommunications member, whose one row is 97. On the page each subtotal equals its rows. No subtotal is published and the published rows equal the filed total, so there is nothing to fix in the data.

The subtotal and its rows sit on members that spell the heading differently, so the check cannot pair them. 2024-06-30: the First Lien Services: Consumer subtotal 328,916 is on the 'Services: Consumer' member, while all its rows but one (CSC Serviceworks, 185) are on members that read 'First Lien Debt Services: FEG, Inc.' and the like, without the word Consumer. 2024-09-30: the Midwest Veterinary second lien loan (35,134) is tagged on a member that begins with the First Lien Services: Consumer heading and then repeats the Second Lien one, which moves three rollups by 35,134 and one by 45,000; and the Metropolis Class A preferred (17,868) is on 'Preferred Equity Consumer' while the subtotal 24,154 is on 'Preferred Equity SERVICES Consumer'. On the page each subtotal equals its rows; the rows are published under the printed lien and industry.

The 10-K for 2024-12-31 tags the 49,277 Accession Risk Management delayed-draw loan on a second Titan Purchaser member under Automotive, so the Banking, Finance, Insurance & Real Estate subtotal 308,744 finds rows of 259,467; the 10-Q for 2025-03-31 repeats those tags in its comparative schedule. The 10-K also carries the prior-year Second Lien Services: Business subtotal 50,363 on a current-period context. The published row is corrected to Accession Risk Management (row correction of D-099) and carries the Banking industry; the member the filer chose cannot be changed, so the check keeps firing.

Position contexts with no fair value fact: members the filer defines for rate and period facts or under an earlier spelling. No value is filed on them; the positions with values tie to the filed total.
Leaves counted without a fair value are comparative-period rows and contexts that carry no fair value fact; the published total equals the filed total.
Leaves counted without a fair value are equity contexts that carry only an acquisition date (duration contexts), comparative-period rows and the superseded 10-K.
Tagged rows with a principal and no fair value are the commitments note, not positions.
About 200 leaf contexts a quarter carry only an acquisition date (duration contexts) and no fair value; the check counts them as positions without a value.
The same printed twin lines counted as duplicate position keys.
Position keys counted as duplicates are tranche twins whose members differ only by a trailing ' One' / ' Two'; each is published as its own row.
Two filings for 2025-12-31: the 10-K 0001193125-26-088367 and the 10-K/A 0001193125-26-096532 (832 rows each); the amendment is the one published.
To 2025-06-30 the filer tags the printed unit count of equity rows as a principal amount, so no share fact exists (36 to 65 rows a quarter); from 2025-09-30 it files share counts.
The one or two equity rows a quarter with no share count are membership interests in the fund's affiliated holding vehicles; the page prints a percentage interest and no unit count.

The schedule has one column, 'Par Amount / Shares', and the filer files no share count for most equity rows (2 to 6 rows a quarter, under 0.5 pct of fair value): the cell is a dash (Xponential, Accession) or its figure is tagged with the principal concept in thousands of dollars. On the preferred rows the figure is an amount, not a count: it grows at the row's PIK rate (Metropolis Class B 6,314, 6,950, 7,535, 8,162). No fix applies: the one wrapper setting that reads a principal tag as a unit count (units_tagged_as_par) would publish 4,000 for the warrant's printed 4 and a dollar amount as a share count for the preferred rows.
Small negative fair values on the same netted commitment rows (the mark on an undrawn line, e.g. 1,628 - 1,679 = -51).
Negative principal, cost and fair value on an undrawn revolver, as printed and tagged.
The spread of 16.00 on Evolve Biologics is the printed spread. (2023-03-31 is not included: the Vice Group Holding spreads of 15.0 in that quarter were not read.)
The same growth from one holding to 27 rows at 2025-03-31.
The same growth of the schedule at 2023-09-30, reported by the row-count check.
Row count 141 to 478 and fair value 984.3M to 1,212.4M between 2023-06-30 and 2023-09-30: the added rows are printed positions and the published total equals the printed total.
The schedule grew from one holding to 27 rows in the first quarter of 2025; published equals the filed total in both quarters.
The same growth of the schedule at 2023-09-30 (many small positions acquired 7/28/2023).

The fourth-quarter 2022 distribution was a regular 0.65 and a special 0.43 a share, 1.08 against 0.57 to 0.63 in the three quarters before; annualised it is 19.83 pct of net asset value against an income ratio of 10.77. Published is the filed figure.
The same growth at 2025-03-31, reported at fund level.
The same growth of the schedule at 2023-09-30, reported at fund level.

The yield the check compares is the filer's ratio of net investment income to average net assets (13.88, 13.96, 13.83). The fund is levered: its investments are 225, 215 and 234 pct of net assets in these quarters, so income over net assets sits above the portfolio's weighted coupon (11.80, 11.84, 11.55) by more than the check's two points. Both sides are as filed; the rates of the largest loans were read against the page in the earlier reading.
Income yield above the weighted coupon while the fund ramps: investments grew from 480M to 2,132M during 2024, so a quarter's income sits over a fast-growing base.
A fund-level row before operations began; net assets 25,000.
The sum of percent of net assets, 234.35, is the filer's printed total; the fund borrows and its investments are 188 to 234 pct of net assets in every quarter.

The check compares rows by issuer name and values. With the tranche words taken out of the name (D-101), two undrawn or zero-value lines of one issuer look alike; they are different members and both are printed.
Rows flagged as duplicates are twin lines the page prints: equal principal and fair value, told apart by a financing-facility footnote. Each is a separate member in the filing and both are positions.

The flagged equity rows are current-period rows of each schedule. The rule tracks them because their unit count, cost and value equal the prior period's. They appeared once the unit counts of these rows were published (D-150). The reason already recorded for this fund (DS-024-1812554) and accepted for Oaktree (DS-N5-PP03-1872371-READ, D-146).

The same IRGSE affiliate roll-forward total, reported by the row check. 2026-03-31 is not included: that quarter also holds the Structured Credit Partners JV row, published through a pinned add rule with fields missing.
The same commitment-table rows, reported by the row check.
The same footnote aggregate on the bare Denali member (760,400 / 782,500 / 1,544,900 / 2,522,500 / 2,657,000 by quarter), reported by the row check.

The source row reported as missing is the printed subtotal of the two LJ Perimeter Buyer lines, which the filer tagged on a member spelled like a position. Rule exclude_2025q1_lj_perimeter_subtotal removes it; both lines are published.

Rows reported as missing are removed on purpose: the look-through schedule of the joint venture North Haven Keystone, LLC (2025-12-31, 2026-03-31; rule exclude_keystone_lookthrough) and the KWOR Acquisition issuer subtotal (2025-03-31, 2025-06-30; rule exclude_kwor_bare_issuer_aggregate).
One row added from the printed page by rule add_missing_atlas_purchaser_first_lien_2025_03: the filing prints the line and tags no fact for it, so it has no source context.
Units that print a dividend rate: TradingScreen / TS Imagine Class AA Units, as labelled by the filer.
An equity row with a PIK rate, as printed and tagged.
An equity-labelled row with a rate: the page itself labels a loan 'Partnership Units'.

After the corrections of D-102 (the OEConnection loan tagged on a McQueen Bidco member; three LLC interests classed as loans) every flagged row is a line of the commitments table: no principal, no rate, fair value zero or negative. An earlier reviewer's 'real error' verdict on these two quarters referred to the rows now corrected.

Loans with no rate and no spread because none is tagged: Sweep Midco second lien (two rows a quarter) is printed with no rate; at 2025-06-30 three non-accrual loans print a rate that the filer did not tag, so the published rows are incomplete as filed.

Principal far above fair value on undrawn commitment rows: by the owner's ruling of 2026-10-10 ('net each loan') such a row keeps the committed amount as principal and publishes cost 0 and the mark as fair value.

Every flagged row (34 in nine quarters, fair value 1 to 162 thousand each) is an undrawn delayed-draw or revolving line. The schedule prints a dash in the Par Amount column and a small fair value, the mark on the commitment; the same figure is in the unfunded-commitments table of the notes. No principal fact is filed on any of the contexts. No fix applies: there is no par on the page to declare.

ARES 2007-3R subordinated notes: the filer reports 20,000,000 in the Shares/Units column, nothing in the Principal column, a dash for cost and a fair value of 0.1M. No principal fact is filed. The count stays a unit count (the reason the owner accepted for Ares Strategic Income, D-151).

Three Sixth Street Lending Partners lines for which the page prints no par and the filing tags no principal: the second Galileo Parent line at 2023-06-30 (the par is printed once for two lines) and the Cordance Operations loan at 2025-06-30 and 2025-09-30, whose par is printed as a dash (an undrawn line carried at a negative cost and a small positive value). The reason the owner accepted for BCRED Pigments Services (D-152).

The six flagged rows are tranches the filer reports in the Shares/Units column with no principal (the reason of DS-X11-1918712). Five carry a share-count fact. The sixth, JPMMT 2026-ACES1, prints 1,405,613,866 in that column and the filer tagged it with its percent-of-shares concept, so the row publishes neither a count nor a par. Not covered by the accepted entry, whose check requires a share-count fact.
The joint venture's look-through rows (2025-12-31 97 rows 249.685M, 2026-03-31 120 rows 294.975M), excluded by rule; their percent is of the joint venture's net assets.
The same IRGSE affiliate roll-forward total, not a position.
The KWOR Acquisition issuer subtotal (2025-03-31, 2025-06-30), excluded by rule.

The rows reported as missing are the filer's separate unfunded-commitments table, removed on purpose (rule exclude_commitment_table_rows). They are outside 'Total Investments' and repeat value already in the schedule.
The same excluded LJ Perimeter Buyer subtotal (19,967, 2025-03-31), reported by the reconciliation's second engine.

The row reported as missing is a footnote aggregate tagged on the Denali member, in millions; rule exclude_denali_bare_duplicate_rows removes it. It equals the sum of the eight equity rows, which are published.

The rows reported are the affiliate roll-forward total for IRGSE Holding Corp. ('Controlled Affiliated Investments', 'IRGSE Holding Corp'). The four IRGSE positions are published and sum to it exactly in every quarter.

From the 10-Q for 2025-03-31 Blue Owl Credit Income keeps the '% of Net Assets' column header and prints no percent on its position rows, and tags none. The filed percent goes from 494 rows to 0; the recomputed percent is published for every row.

From the 10-K for 2024-12-31 Blue Owl Credit Income tags the rows of its commitments table (about 220 undrawn lines a quarter). That table prints a commitment type, an expiration date, the funded and unfunded commitment and a fair value: no cost, no maturity, no industry and no percent of net assets. Coverage of those four fields falls from 100 to about 69 pct because these rows were added, not because a field was lost on the position rows. The rows are published under the owner's ruling 'keep the undrawn lines'.
Spreads are printed including a credit spread adjustment, so they are not quarter-point values.
The same negative principal on undrawn revolvers, as tagged.
The dollar copy of the same negative principal.
The fund is an infrastructure fund that files as a BDC: about three quarters of net assets is equity in holding vehicles for infrastructure assets, as the schedule prints.

Published equals the printed 'Total Investments at fair value' exactly in the three quarters. The check adds a cash-equivalents figure to the filed investments line, but from 2025-06-30 that line already includes the money market fund, and the fund-level cash-equivalents figure it adds (62,915,000) is the 2024-12-31 balance carried forward.
A fund-level row of 2022-03-31, before the first published schedule (2023-03-31); no holdings are published for it.
One loan, Ligado Networks LLC (fair value 1.8M to 4.7M, on non-accrual), is printed and tagged with its original maturity of 11/1/2023 in every later filing. Published is the page.
A context that holds only a loan's rate facts, joined to the sibling context that holds its values (rate_only_contexts, D-103); the rate-only context is then removed by design.
The same page-added Atlas Purchaser row (1.09M): there is no tag to verify it against.
The 23 rows flagged non-accrual at 2025-12-31 carry a cost of 8.60M, the figure the filing prints for non-accrual investments.
The filer prints percent of net assets to one decimal; the rows that differ from fair value over net assets by more than 0.1 are the filer's own printed figures. Published is the page.
The filer prints percent of net assets to one decimal; one to eight rows a quarter differ from fair value over net assets by 0.11 to 0.15 points. Published is the printed figure.

One row of 99, 134 and 149: the percent is printed to one decimal and the tag carries that rounded figure (0.1 on a fair value of 378; -0.1 on -11 and -82). Published is the tag. The reason accepted for Blue Owl Credit Income (rounding floor).
The filer prints and tags two percents on the wrong rows of one issuer. Published is the tag.

One row at 2025-09-30 (of 152 tested): the page prints the percent as '0.1 7' across two cells and the filer tagged the first cell, 0.1. Published is the tag; fair value over net assets gives 0.17. No fix applies: percent of net assets is not a field a row correction or a declared value may set.
One row of 631: the page reader took the cell 'S + 7.00 % PIK' as no reference rate; the published SOFR is what the page and the member print.
